audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 16, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, archaeological, and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for dynastic curse, corpse exposure, alcohol context, assassination, household extermination, seven-day rule, siege, Zimri's self-inflicted death by fire, civil conflict, Samaria land purchase, Ahab and Jezebel, anti-foreign-wife scapegoating, religious persecution risk, and deaths of Hiel's sons.

verses.restored: Word of YHWH came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:
Because I raised you from dust and made you leader over my people Israel, but you walked in way of Jeroboam and made my people Israel sin, provoking me with their sins,
look, I will sweep away Baasha and his house and make your house like house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
One belonging to Baasha who dies in city dogs shall eat, and one who dies in field birds of heavens shall eat.
Rest of acts of Baasha, what he did, and his might—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?
Baasha lay with his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah. Elah his son reigned in his place.

Also by hand of prophet Jehu son of Hanani word of YHWH came against Baasha and his house, for all evil he did in eyes of YHWH, provoking YHWH with work of his hands, becoming like house of Jeroboam, and because he killed it/him.
In twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha began to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
His servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him while he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk in house of Arza, who was over household in Tirzah.
Zimri came, struck him, and killed him in twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
When he began to reign and sat upon throne, he struck all house of Baasha. He left him no male—literally, one who urinates against wall—neither kinsman nor friend.
Zimri destroyed all house of Baasha according to word of YHWH spoken against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
for all sins of Baasha and sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned and made Israel sin, provoking YHWH, Divine of Israel, with their vanities.
Rest of acts of Elah and all he did—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?
In twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. The people were camped against Gibbethon belonging to Philistines.
The camped people heard, Zimri conspired and also killed king. All Israel made Omri, commander of army, king over Israel that day in camp.
Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
When Zimri saw city was captured, he entered citadel of king's house, burned king's house over himself with fire, and died.
For sins he sinned, doing evil in eyes of YHWH, walking in way of Jeroboam and his sin by which he made Israel sin.
Rest of acts of Zimri and conspiracy he conspired—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?
Then people of Israel were divided into two halves: half people followed Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half followed Omri.
People following Omri prevailed over people following Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
In thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri began to reign over Israel twelve years; six years he reigned in Tirzah.
He bought hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, built upon hill, and called name of city he built Samaria, after name of Shemer, owner of hill.
Omri did evil in eyes of YHWH and did worse than all before him.
He walked in all way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in sin by which he made Israel sin, provoking YHWH, Divine of Israel, with their vanities.
Rest of acts of Omri, what he did, and might he showed—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?
Omri lay with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria. Ahab his son reigned in his place.
In thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, Ahab son of Omri began to reign over Israel. Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did evil in eyes of YHWH beyond all before him.
As though walking in sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat were a light thing, he took as wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of Sidonians, went and served Baal, and bowed to him.
He raised an altar for Baal in house of Baal he built in Samaria.
Ahab made an Asherah. Ahab did more to provoke YHWH, Divine of Israel, than all kings of Israel before him.
In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. With Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and with Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to word of YHWH spoken by Joshua son of Nun.

translation_notes: Dynastic judgment again takes the form of household extermination and corpse exposure. These are not ethical models for political transition or accountability.
Elah is assassinated while intoxicated, but alcohol does not cause or justify Zimri's violence. Substance use must not become victim-blaming.

Zimri's seven-day reign begins with massacre and ends when he burns the palace over himself. His death is a suicide under siege and political collapse, not a heroic model or proof that all suicidal deaths are Divine punishment.
The text immediately moralizes Zimri's death through his sins. Modern readers must not shame people with suicidal thoughts, people who die by suicide, or bereaved families.
The succession from Zimri to Omri passes through military acclamation, siege, civil division, and Tibni's death. Political stability emerges from violence, not consensus.
Samaria's founding includes a land purchase from Shemer. The transaction does not reveal the status of other residents or whether the sale transferred communal rights.

Jezebel is identified as a Sidonian princess and associated with Ahab's Baal policy, but Ahab is the ruling actor who marries, builds, serves, and establishes the cult. Her gender and foreignness must not carry his responsibility.
Baal and Asherah polemic may not justify violence against living religious communities, vandalism, or xenophobia.

The deaths of Hiel's sons at Jericho's foundation and gates may reflect curse fulfillment, construction sacrifice tradition, or compressed family tragedy. Child death must never be treated as an acceptable building cost or ritual offering.
safety_note: Do not romanticize assassination, dynastic massacre, palace self-burning, civil war, or child death. Do not blame alcohol, Jezebel's gender, Sidonian identity, or minority religion for royal violence. Handle Zimri's death with suicide-safe language and compassion.
